CoolfFly Nails the First-Ever Personal eVTOL Inter-Island Flight in the Maldives
8 photos
Photo: CoolFly
No speedboats, no choppers, no traffic, and no harmful emissions – this is what the future of tourist air mobility could like in popular island destinations like the Maldives, and this personal electric aircraft from China is already ahead of the game.
CoolFly, the Chinese brand behind what promises to be one of the most exciting lineup of personal aircraft, is wasting no time in proving what its products are capable of. Most recently, the Hangzhou-based company has enjoyed a very prosperous debut in the Maldives, complete with flight demonstrations that are making history.
It all happened during three full days of public demonstrations, organized by the Ministry of Development, Transportation, and Commerce in Maldives, together with the Chinese embassy in Maldives. CoolFly has also attended Expo Maldives 2026, a fruitful event that ended in two strategic collaborations for the Chinese brand – one with aviation operator Skyline Aviation, and another with CMBGA, a Chinese-Maldivian commercial association.
The highlight of this Maldives debut was the demonstration flight over open water, carried out impeccably by the Dream ST, CoolFly’s personal eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing). The aircraft flew from Malé to Villimalé, covering just under two miles (3 km) over open water.
This was heralded as the first-ever inter-island flight carried out by a personal eVTOL in the Maldives, demonstrating a new era of air mobility – faster, cleaner, more efficient, and a lot more exciting.
Maldives officials are obviously interested in the potential of aircraft like the CoolFly Dream ST for the future of island mobility, and this first step could lead to very exciting prospects – perhaps not too far in the future, these Chinese personal eVTOLs will become a regular sight in the Maldives islands.
In terms of regulations, the Dream ST (Seated Configuration) falls under the FAA Part 103 Ultra-Light aircraft category. Purpose-built for individual flight, the Dream ST combines foldable design for easy transport with all-electric propulsion and a complex safety system.
The proprietary NA80 flight control system promises a seamless flight experience, backed by s two redundant flight control units, each featuring three aviation-grade “inertial measurement units” (IMUs), for millisecond-level fault detection. The Dream ST is intended for short-distance flights of 20 to 30 minutes, boasting a maximum speed of 43 mph (70 kph), coupled with a maximum capacity of 110 kg (242 lbs).
CoolFly’s unique lineup of personal aircraft also includes the Urban, a unique standing-configuration model also built for individual flight. There’s also the Dream Pro, a beefed-up version of the Dream ST, targeting other sectors beyond personal aviation, including multiple defense applications.
This past summer, CoolFly has officially introduced the Dream ST to the American public at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh, and is currently looking to establish an official distribution network across the US, as well as other continents.
